original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: At the #4100 dyadic carve, physical half-bandwidth W and at least W retained coordinates between successive interiors, the Schur complement in boundary order has bandwidth at most 2W-1. This matches the one-interval cap and justifies the written O(W) claim. The constant is sharp. A separator of W-1 coordinates can make the bandwidth grow with the number of interiors.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified #4100 implication at its caller. The chosen implication is the precision/conditioning bandwidth of the separated carve, not CRT repair, the free-algebra lift, or fixed-tape induction. Those remain open.
bottleneck_link: The O(W) Schur band is what keeps the carved boundary cost inside the #4100 Gaussian allowance. The audit confirms that band at the sharp cap 2W-1. It does not change a supplier moment or the selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop once the boundary-order cap is proved for separators of at least b survivors and the shorter-separator counterexample is certified. Do not reprice Strassen or audit another #4100 partition.
evidence: Exact rational checks: the #4285 7x7 witness attains bandwidth 3 with far entry -1/432; separated layouts of bandwidth 1, 2 and 3 stay within 2b-1 and a two-interval host attains it; the bandwidth-2 chain with one survivor between singleton interiors has Schur bandwidth equal to the interior count for 1..8 interiors. Counting argument in README.md. Verifier prints PASS gaussian-carve-schur-bandwidth.

open_questions.question: Does any narrow boundary solve on this Schur complement use triangular windows of width exactly W?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A window of width W misses the sharp 2W-1 fill. The O(W) cost sentence would still be true, but that solver would be the wrong band.
open_questions.first_step: Bind one narrow solve in the retained shallow-Toeplitz schedule to a concrete window width and compare it with 2W-1.
open_questions.blocked_by: GAUSSIAN.md states O(W) and an RHS batch of width at most 2W. It does not name an executable triangular-window width.

open_questions.question: Does every #4100 phase cell retain a period cut through elimination?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A circular cell with no retained cut is the setting where Schur bandwidth can follow arc length instead of the linear cap 2W-1.
open_questions.first_step: Take one full-period cell in the caller and mark its period cut as boundary before the carve.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package audits the linear capped-interior loop and does not replay the tensor caller.
